name: (ADFS) Lifecycle Manager
description: Retention, archiving and deletion policies for file/media entities, evaluated automatically via cron and the Queue API. Provides a LifecycleAction plugin type, a lifecycle_policy config entity, legal hold, an audit log, per-policy webhooks and Drush commands. Sub-module of Advanced Filesystem.
project_description: The Lifecycle Manager sub-module of Advanced Filesystem manages the retention of file and media entities through configurable policies. A lifecycle_policy config entity pairs conditions (entity type, bundles, MIME types, size range, minimum age, EXIF-metadata presence, referencing entity/field, current lifecycle status) with actions (archive after N days/hours/minutes to another stream wrapper, delete after N with soft or hard mode, strip metadata on archive, notify roles, fire a webhook). PolicyEvaluator decides whether each entity matches; LifecycleManagerService evaluates enabled policies in priority order and enqueues matching entities into the lifecycle_manager queue, where LifecycleQueueWorker applies the resolved LifecycleAction plugin (archive_to_storage, delete_file, restore_file, notify_user, strip_metadata). Evaluation runs on cron (with optional per-policy day/hour schedules and a cron_limit), from the Run form, or via Drush (lifecycle:run, lifecycle:status, lifecycle:queue-size, lifecycle:reset-stats). Three base fields are installed on the file entity: adfs_lifecycle_status (active/archived/deleted/legal_hold), adfs_last_accessed (updated by hook_file_download) and adfs_original_uri (for restore). Every applied action is written to the lifecycle_audit_log table by LifecycleAuditLogger and viewable/clearable in the UI; files can be placed on legal hold to exempt them from all policies; a per-policy webhook is POSTed via a WebhookEventSubscriber when an action is applied. All administration is gated behind the restricted 'administer lifecycle_policies' permission (audit-log viewing also accepts 'view lifecycle audit log').
